FAILURE CASES CAPTURED: (1) required fields show a red exclamation icon and the Save button stays disabled client-side, no server round-trip possible, until both Customer Type and Description are filled -- pure client-side gating, confirmed no network request fires on a disabled-Save click; (2) typing a code that collides with an existing real record shows an inline red tooltip 'This customer type has already existed' directly under the field, entirely client-side (no network request accompanies it -- checked via read_network_requests, confirmed zero matching calls), presumably validated against a locally-cached grid store; (3) BROWSER-AUTOMATION TRAP: after repeated Add-form re-entries within one page session (caused by dismissing harmless nav-glitch 'Processing completed without exception' dialogs and retrying), Ext.ComponentQuery found TWO 'saveButton' component instances, one stale-disabled -- the visible button can get stuck permanently disabled with a fully valid form and zero invalid fields (confirmed via Ext.ComponentQuery walking every form field's isValid()). This did NOT reproduce on a clean single Add-form load. LESSON: if Save stays disabled despite a filled valid form, a full SPA navigation (not just page reload -- that broke the OAuth session, see below) back to the grid then Add again clears it; querying Ext.ComponentQuery.query("button") for duplicate itemId:'saveButton' instances is the reliable diagnostic. SEPARATE GOTCHA: a plain browser page reload (not a SPA route change) on this app invalidates the OIDC session and drops to a full re-login screen -- never use a raw page reload to 'reset' a stuck form, always navigate to a known-good in-app route instead.

trigger: FAILURE CASE RETROFIT: UI Add form with duplicate real client Name (----) + a fresh throwaway Address, Save
verify_method: network capture of both POST responses; found and deleted the resulting orphan address via a follow-up GET filtered by addressName then a direct authenticated DELETE
notes: CRITICAL FINDING, differs from Suppliers: this create cascade is NOT atomic. The addresses POST fires and SUCCEEDS (201, real address A000365882 created) BEFORE the clients POST is attempted and fails with 422 Unprocessable Entity 'Record already exists.' -- leaving a genuine ORPHAN ADDRESS RECORD in the system on every failed duplicate-client create attempt. Contrast directly with Suppliers (see suppliers.md), where the supplier-uniqueness check apparently runs before addresses POST is ever attempted, so a failed duplicate leaves zero orphans. Found and cleaned up the orphan via GET /wm/addresses?query=[{addressName EQ 'ZZAudit Dup Test'}] then DELETE /wm/addresses/{id} with the live CSRF token. THIRD distinct duplicate-key error shape across three sibling Partners screens tested so far: Customer Types (pure client-side, zero network calls), Suppliers (clean 409 Conflict, no orphan), Clients (422 Unprocessable Entity, WITH an orphan side-effect). Never assume cascade atomicity holds for any screen without testing that screen's failure path directly -- a proven-clean cascade on one screen says nothing about a sibling screen's cascade.

notes: FOURTH duplicate-key validation architecture seen across Partners sibling screens: Customer Types (client-side, tooltip visible), Suppliers (server-side 409, no orphan), Clients (server-side 422, WITH an orphan address -- see clients.md), and now Existing Customers (client-side gate again, like Customer Types, but no tooltip text captured this time -- Save simply stays permanently disabled with a red icon on the Customer field for a known-duplicate value, confirmed zero network calls). Four sibling Partners screens, four different combinations of client-side-vs-server-side validation and atomic-vs-non-atomic cascade behavior for the exact same conceptual error (duplicate primary key on create). trigger: BROWSER-AUTOMATION TECHNIQUE NOTE (not a write test): investigating why mouse-wheel scroll on the Add form appeared to do nothing on repeated attempts
verify_method: DOM inspection via javascript_tool inside the app iframe
notes: ROOT CAUSE of a recurring 'scroll does nothing' symptom seen on several Add/Edit forms across this app: the scrollable region is an ExtJS-internal div (class x-panel-body, found via querySelectorAll('div.x-panel-body') filtering for scrollHeight > clientHeight), NOT the outer page body -- confirmed one instance at iframe-relative rect {x:16,y:90,w:710,h:607} with scrollHeight 978 vs clientHeight 605/553. Synthetic mouse-wheel scroll events at plausible page coordinates did NOT reliably move this container across multiple attempts (screenshots identical before/after). Directly setting el.scrollTop via javascript_tool DID move it reliably and immediately, confirmed by a subsequent screenshot showing different form fields in view. The Save/Cancel footer bar stays pinned OUTSIDE this scrollable body at a fixed page position regardless of scroll state, so Save's click coordinate does not need to be re-derived after scrolling -- only the fields above it move. RECOMMENDATION for any future executor automating a long Add/Edit form on this app: if a target field isn't visible and mouse-wheel scroll isn't moving it, locate the real x-panel-body scroll container via DOM query and set scrollTop directly rather than retrying wheel events blindly.
